---
title: "NDIS Payments Rose 12%; Published Utilisation Edged Down"
description: "Trailing-12-month NDIS payments rose by $5.6 billion to June 2026. Participant numbers and budgets increased, while the published national utilisation rate edged down."
date: "2026-05-26"
date-modified: "2026-10-13"
categories: [ndis, disability, public-spending, australia]
author: "Aydin"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)
library(forcats)
library(scales)
library(knitr)

source(file.path("..", "..", "R", "data_sources.R"))

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.caption.position = "plot",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
)

raw_dir <- "data-raw"
source_registry <- read_source_registry("sources.csv")
source_files <- lapply(
  seq_len(nrow(source_registry)),
  function(index) download_registered_source(source_registry[index, , drop = FALSE], raw_dir)
)
source_manifest <- write_source_manifest(source_files, file.path(raw_dir, "source-manifest.csv"))

source_path <- function(source_id) {
  index <- match(source_id, source_registry$source_id)
  if (is.na(index)) stop("Missing source in sources.csv: ", source_id, call. = FALSE)
  source_files[[index]]$path
}

clean_names <- function(x) {
  x |>
    str_to_lower() |>
    str_replace_all("&", "and") |>
    str_replace_all("[^a-z0-9]+", "_") |>
    str_replace_all("^_|_$", "")
}

as_number <- function(x) {
  if (is.numeric(x)) return(x)
  parse_number(as.character(x), na = c("", "NA", "na", "n/a", "<11"))
}

as_rate <- function(x) {
  value <- as_number(x)
  ifelse(value > 1.5, value / 100, value)
}

assert_true <- function(condition, message) {
  if (!isTRUE(condition)) stop(message, call. = FALSE)
}

read_registered_csv <- function(source_id) {
  data <- read_csv(
    source_path(source_id),
    show_col_types = FALSE,
    na = c("", "NA", "na", "n/a")
  )
  names(data) <- clean_names(names(data))
  data
}

parse_budget <- function(source_id, period) {
  data <- read_registered_csv(source_id)
  required <- c(
    "rprtdt", "statecd", "srvcdstrctnm", "dsbltygrpnm", "agebnd",
    "suppclass", "avganlsdcmtdsuppbdgt", "actvprtcpnt"
  )
  assert_true(all(required %in% names(data)), paste("Budget schema changed for", period))

  national <- data |>
    filter(
      statecd == "ALL", srvcdstrctnm == "ALL", dsbltygrpnm == "ALL",
      agebnd == "ALL", suppclass == "ALL"
    )
  assert_true(nrow(national) == 1, paste("Expected one national budget row for", period))

  national |>
    transmute(
      period,
      report_date = as.Date(rprtdt, "%d%b%Y"),
      participants = as_number(actvprtcpnt),
      average_budget = as_number(avganlsdcmtdsuppbdgt)
    )
}

parse_utilisation <- function(source_id, period) {
  data <- read_registered_csv(source_id)
  required <- c(
    "rprtdt", "statecd", "srvcdstrctnm", "dsbltygrpnm", "agebnd",
    "silorsda", "suppclass", "utlstn"
  )
  assert_true(all(required %in% names(data)), paste("Utilisation schema changed for", period))

  national <- data |>
    filter(
      statecd == "ALL", srvcdstrctnm == "ALL", dsbltygrpnm == "ALL",
      agebnd == "ALL", silorsda == "ALL", suppclass == "ALL"
    )
  assert_true(nrow(national) == 1, paste("Expected one national utilisation row for", period))

  national |>
    transmute(
      period,
      report_date = as.Date(rprtdt, "%d%b%Y"),
      utilisation = as_rate(utlstn)
    )
}

parse_payments <- function(source_id, period) {
  data <- read_registered_csv(source_id)
  required <- c(
    "rprtdt", "suppclass", "suppcatnm", "suppitemnmbr", "suppitemdesc",
    "rsdsinstatecd", "rsdsinsrvcdstrctnm", "ndisdsbltygrpnm",
    "ndiaagebnd", "pmtamt"
  )
  assert_true(all(required %in% names(data)), paste("Payments schema changed for", period))

  data <- data |>
    mutate(payment_amount = as_number(pmtamt))

  national_support <- data |>
    filter(
      suppcatnm == "ALL", suppitemnmbr == "ALL", suppitemdesc == "ALL",
      rsdsinstatecd == "ALL", rsdsinsrvcdstrctnm == "ALL",
      ndisdsbltygrpnm == "ALL", ndiaagebnd == "ALL"
    ) |>
    transmute(
      period,
      report_date = as.Date(rprtdt, "%d-%b-%y"),
      support_class = suppclass,
      payment_amount
    )

  assert_true(
    identical(sort(unique(national_support$support_class)), sort(c("Capacity Building", "Capital", "Core", "Missing"))),
    paste("Unexpected national support classes for", period)
  )
  assert_true(!anyDuplicated(national_support$support_class), paste("Duplicate national support classes for", period))
  assert_true(all(is.finite(national_support$payment_amount)), paste("Missing national payment amount for", period))
  expected_date <- if (period == "June 2025") as.Date("2025-06-30") else as.Date("2026-06-30")
  assert_true(all(national_support$report_date == expected_date), paste("Unexpected payment report date for", period))

  national_disability_cells <- data |>
    filter(
      suppcatnm == "ALL", suppitemnmbr == "ALL", suppitemdesc == "ALL",
      rsdsinstatecd == "ALL", rsdsinsrvcdstrctnm == "ALL",
      ndisdsbltygrpnm != "ALL", ndiaagebnd == "ALL"
    )

  assert_true(
    all(as.Date(national_disability_cells$rprtdt, "%d-%b-%y") == expected_date),
    paste("Unexpected disability-payment report date for", period)
  )
  disability_cell_counts <- national_disability_cells |>
    count(ndisdsbltygrpnm, suppclass) |>
    arrange(ndisdsbltygrpnm, suppclass)
  assert_true(
    nrow(filter(disability_cell_counts, n > 1, ndisdsbltygrpnm != "Missing")) == 0,
    paste("Duplicate classified disability/support-class rows for", period)
  )
  nonmissing_structure <- national_disability_cells |>
    filter(ndisdsbltygrpnm != "Missing") |>
    count(ndisdsbltygrpnm, suppclass)
  assert_true(
    nrow(nonmissing_structure) == 17 * 4 &&
      all(nonmissing_structure$n == 1) &&
      setequal(unique(nonmissing_structure$suppclass), c("Capacity Building", "Capital", "Core", "Missing")),
    paste("Unexpected disability/support-class structure for", period)
  )
  expected_missing_structure <- if (period == "June 2025") {
    tibble(suppclass = c("Capacity Building", "Capital", "Core", "Missing"), n = c(2L, 1L, 2L, 2L))
  } else {
    tibble(suppclass = c("Capacity Building", "Capital", "Core", "Missing"), n = rep(2L, 4))
  }
  observed_missing_structure <- disability_cell_counts |>
    filter(ndisdsbltygrpnm == "Missing") |>
    select(suppclass, n) |>
    arrange(suppclass)
  expected_missing_structure <- expected_missing_structure |>
    arrange(suppclass)
  assert_true(
    identical(observed_missing_structure, expected_missing_structure),
    paste("Unexpected Missing-group disability/support-class rows for", period)
  )
  expected_suppressed <- if (period == "June 2025") 3L else 1L
  suppressed_cells <- national_disability_cells |>
    filter(is.na(payment_amount))
  assert_true(
    nrow(suppressed_cells) == expected_suppressed &&
      all(suppressed_cells$ndisdsbltygrpnm == "Missing"),
    paste("Unexpected number of suppressed national disability payment cells for", period)
  )

  national_disability <- national_disability_cells |>
    group_by(ndisdsbltygrpnm) |>
    summarise(payment_amount = sum(payment_amount, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    transmute(period, disability_group = ndisdsbltygrpnm, payment_amount)

  total_support <- sum(national_support$payment_amount)
  total_disability <- sum(national_disability$payment_amount)
  residual <- total_support - total_disability
  assert_true(
    residual >= 0 && residual / total_support < 0.001,
    paste("Disability-payment reconciliation residual is unexpectedly large for", period)
  )
  national_disability <- bind_rows(
    national_disability,
    tibble(
      period,
      disability_group = "Suppression/reconciliation residual",
      payment_amount = residual
    )
  )
  assert_true(
    abs(total_support - sum(national_disability$payment_amount)) < 1e-8 * total_support,
    paste("National support and disability totals do not reconcile for", period)
  )

  list(support = national_support, disability = national_disability)
}

budget <- bind_rows(
  parse_budget("ndis_budget_2025_06", "June 2025"),
  parse_budget("ndis_budget_2026_06", "June 2026")
)
utilisation <- bind_rows(
  parse_utilisation("ndis_utilisation_2025_06", "June 2025"),
  parse_utilisation("ndis_utilisation_2026_06", "June 2026")
)
payments_2025 <- parse_payments("ndis_payments_2025_06", "June 2025")
payments_2026 <- parse_payments("ndis_payments_2026_06", "June 2026")
support_payments <- bind_rows(payments_2025$support, payments_2026$support)
disability_payments <- bind_rows(payments_2025$disability, payments_2026$disability)

assert_true(all(budget$report_date == as.Date(c("2025-06-30", "2026-06-30"))), "Budget report dates changed.")
assert_true(all(utilisation$report_date == as.Date(c("2025-06-30", "2026-06-30"))), "Utilisation report dates changed.")
assert_true(all(between(utilisation$utilisation, 0, 1)), "National utilisation falls outside 0 to 1.")
assert_true(all(budget$participants > 0 & budget$average_budget > 0), "National budget values must be positive.")

payment_totals <- support_payments |>
  group_by(period) |>
  summarise(total_payments = sum(payment_amount), .groups = "drop")

support_change <- support_payments |>
  select(period, support_class, payment_amount) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = period, values_from = payment_amount, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(change = `June 2026` - `June 2025`)

headline <- tibble(
  payment_start = payment_totals$total_payments[payment_totals$period == "June 2025"],
  payment_end = payment_totals$total_payments[payment_totals$period == "June 2026"],
  participants_start = budget$participants[budget$period == "June 2025"],
  participants_end = budget$participants[budget$period == "June 2026"],
  budget_start = budget$average_budget[budget$period == "June 2025"],
  budget_end = budget$average_budget[budget$period == "June 2026"],
  utilisation_start = utilisation$utilisation[utilisation$period == "June 2025"],
  utilisation_end = utilisation$utilisation[utilisation$period == "June 2026"]
) |>
  mutate(
    payment_change = payment_end - payment_start,
    payment_growth = payment_end / payment_start - 1,
    participant_growth = participants_end / participants_start - 1,
    budget_growth = budget_end / budget_start - 1,
    utilisation_change = utilisation_end - utilisation_start
  )

core_change_share <- support_change |>
  filter(support_class == "Core") |>
  summarise(value = change / headline$payment_change) |>
  pull(value)
support_change_value <- function(class) support_change$change[support_change$support_class == class]

disability_change <- disability_payments |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = period, values_from = payment_amount) |>
  mutate(change = `June 2026` - `June 2025`) |>
  arrange(desc(change))

assert_true(!anyNA(disability_change[c("June 2025", "June 2026")]), "Disability groups do not align across payment releases.")
assert_true(headline$payment_change > 0, "Expected a positive national payment change.")
top_two_share <- disability_change |>
  slice_max(change, n = 2, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  summarise(value = sum(change) / headline$payment_change) |>
  pull(value)
top_five_share <- disability_change |>
  slice_max(change, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  summarise(value = sum(change) / headline$payment_change) |>
  pull(value)
assert_true(between(top_two_share, 0, 1) && between(top_five_share, 0, 1), "Contribution shares fall outside 0 to 1.")
autism_change <- disability_change$change[disability_change$disability_group == "Autism"]
intellectual_disability_change <- disability_change$change[disability_change$disability_group == "Intellectual Disability"]
```

NDIS payments increased sharply in the year to June 2026. The national payment measure rose by `r dollar(headline$payment_change, scale = 1e-9, suffix = " billion", accuracy = 0.1)`—`r percent(headline$payment_growth, accuracy = 0.1)`—to `r dollar(headline$payment_end, scale = 1e-9, suffix = " billion", accuracy = 0.1)`.

Over the same June-to-June comparison, active participants increased `r percent(headline$participant_growth, accuracy = 0.1)`, the published average annualised committed support budget increased by about `r percent(round(headline$budget_growth, 2), accuracy = 1)`, and the national utilisation rate slipped from `r percent(headline$utilisation_start, accuracy = 1)` to `r percent(headline$utilisation_end, accuracy = 1)`. The budget average is rounded to the nearest $1,000, so its growth rate is approximate.

Those measures do not form a mechanical decomposition: they describe different time windows. But they do not support one simple story. The latest payment growth did **not** coincide with a rise in the published national utilisation rate.

## The payment measure is annual, not quarterly

The payments files report the preceding 12 months at each reporting date. Comparing June with June therefore gives two aligned annual windows. The old version of this analysis called these figures quarterly payments, which overstated the pace of change because adjacent quarterly releases contain nine months of overlapping activity.

Core supports account for `r percent(core_change_share, accuracy = 1)` of the national increase. They rose by `r dollar(support_change_value("Core"), scale = 1e-9, suffix = " billion", accuracy = 0.1)`, compared with `r dollar(support_change_value("Capacity Building"), scale = 1e-9, suffix = " billion", accuracy = 0.1)` for capacity building and `r dollar(support_change_value("Capital"), scale = 1e-9, suffix = " billion", accuracy = 0.1)` for capital supports.

```{r}
#| label: payments-by-support-class
#| fig-cap: "Contribution to the change in trailing-12-month NDIS payments by support class, June 2025 to June 2026. The small Missing/unclassified category is retained as published so totals reconcile."
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal bars show core supports contributing about 4.6 billion dollars of the 5.6 billion dollar increase, capacity building 0.8 billion, and capital 0.2 billion."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.8

support_plot <- support_change |>
  mutate(
    support_class = fct_reorder(support_class, change),
    direction = if_else(change >= 0, "Increase", "Decrease"),
    change_label = if_else(
      abs(change) < 5e7,
      NA_character_,
      dollar(change, scale = 1e-9, suffix = "b", accuracy = 0.1)
    )
  )

ggplot(support_plot, aes(change, support_class, fill = direction)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_col(width = 0.66) +
  geom_text(aes(label = change_label), hjust = if_else(support_plot$change >= 0, -0.15, 1.15), size = 3.6) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_dollar(scale = 1e-9, suffix = "b"), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.13))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Increase = "#16735c", Decrease = "#b0433c")) +
  labs(x = "Contribution to annual payment change", y = NULL, fill = NULL)
```

## Scale grew; the published utilisation rate edged down

The national aggregate rows provide the cleanest comparison. They avoid double-counting people who appear under multiple support classes, and they avoid treating thousands of detailed cells as equally important.

By June 2026, the Scheme had `r comma(headline$participants_end)` active participants, up from `r comma(headline$participants_start)`. The average annualised committed support budget rose from `r dollar(headline$budget_start)` to `r dollar(headline$budget_end)`.

Utilisation needs a timing warning. The June 2026 figure covers supports delivered from October 2025 to March 2026 and paid by 30 June. It is a lagged six-month measure, not June-quarter utilisation. On that official national measure, utilisation fell by `r number(abs(100 * headline$utilisation_change), accuracy = 1)` percentage point.

```{r}
#| label: national-indicators
#| fig-cap: "Change from June 2025 to June 2026 in four national NDIS indicators. Utilisation is shown as a percentage-point change; the other three are percentage changes. Budget growth is approximate because the published averages are rounded to the nearest $1,000."
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal bars show payments rising 12.2 percent, participant numbers rising 5.8 percent, average annualised support budgets rising about 2 percent, and national utilisation falling by one percentage point."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.8

kpi_change <- tibble(
  metric = c(
    "Payments (trailing 12 months)",
    "Active participants",
    "Average annualised support budget",
    "National utilisation (lagged six months)"
  ),
  change = c(
    100 * headline$payment_growth,
    100 * headline$participant_growth,
    round(100 * headline$budget_growth),
    100 * headline$utilisation_change
  ),
  label = c(
    percent(headline$payment_growth, accuracy = 0.1),
    percent(headline$participant_growth, accuracy = 0.1),
    str_c("about ", percent(round(headline$budget_growth, 2), accuracy = 1)),
    str_c("-", number(abs(100 * headline$utilisation_change), accuracy = 0.1), " pp")
  )
  ) |>
  mutate(
    metric = fct_reorder(metric, change),
    direction = if_else(change >= 0, "Increase", "Decrease"),
    label_x = if_else(change >= 0, change, 0.12)
  )

ggplot(kpi_change, aes(change, metric, fill = direction)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_col(width = 0.62) +
  geom_text(aes(x = label_x, label = label), hjust = -0.18, size = 3.7) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = "%"), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.12, 0.14))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Increase = "#246b8e", Decrease = "#b0433c")) +
  labs(x = "Change (percentage points for utilisation; percent for other indicators)", y = NULL, fill = NULL)
```

## Half the payment increase sits in two disability groups

The annual payment increase was also concentrated by primary disability group. Autism contributed `r dollar(autism_change, scale = 1e-9, suffix = " billion", accuracy = 0.01)` and intellectual disability `r dollar(intellectual_disability_change, scale = 1e-9, suffix = " billion", accuracy = 0.01)`. Together they account for `r percent(top_two_share, accuracy = 1)` of the **net national increase**; the five largest positive contributors account for `r percent(top_five_share, accuracy = 1)`.

This is an accounting contribution, not a causal finding. It combines changes in participant numbers, support mix, prices, payment timing and average payments. The chart does not explain why any disability-group total changed.

```{r}
#| label: disability-contributions
#| fig-cap: "Change in trailing-12-month NDIS payments by primary disability group, June 2025 to June 2026. A small residual reconciles suppressed or unallocated cells to the national total."
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal bars show autism contributing about 1.75 billion dollars and intellectual disability about 1.01 billion dollars to annual payment growth. Developmental delay records the largest decline."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7

disability_plot <- disability_change |>
  mutate(
    disability_group = recode(
      disability_group,
      "ABI" = "Acquired brain injury",
      "Other Neurological" = "Other neurological",
      "Cerebral Palsy" = "Cerebral palsy"
    ),
    disability_group = fct_reorder(disability_group, change),
    emphasis = case_when(
      disability_group %in% c("Autism", "Intellectual Disability") ~ "Largest two contributors",
      change < 0 ~ "Decrease",
      TRUE ~ "Other increase"
    ),
    contribution_label = if_else(
      disability_group %in% c("Autism", "Intellectual Disability"),
      dollar(change, scale = 1e-9, suffix = "b", accuracy = 0.01),
      NA_character_
    )
  )

ggplot(disability_plot, aes(change, disability_group, fill = emphasis)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_col(width = 0.72) +
  geom_text(aes(label = contribution_label), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.4, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = label_dollar(scale = 1e-9, suffix = "b", accuracy = 0.1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.13))
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Largest two contributors" = "#116b58", "Other increase" = "#8cb9aa", "Decrease" = "#b0433c")) +
  labs(x = "Contribution to annual payment change", y = NULL, fill = NULL)
```

## What this changes about the story

The strongest public-data conclusion is descriptive and fairly narrow. In the year to June 2026, NDIS payments grew faster than either participant numbers or the average committed support budget. The published national utilisation rate did not rise. Most of the dollar increase was in core supports, and about half was associated with two large disability groups.

That does not identify why need, plan values or payments changed. The public extracts are rounded and suppress small cells, and their reporting windows differ. A participant-level causal model would require data these files do not contain. For that reason, this refresh removes the earlier random-forest models and regional joins rather than presenting cross-sectional prediction as an explanation of national payment growth.

The companion analysis asks a different question: [where reported participant outcomes changed after entry to the Scheme](../ndis-outcomes-spend-service-access/).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Sources and reproducibility"}

The analysis uses the NDIA's [participant plan budget and utilisation datasets](https://dataresearch.ndis.gov.au/datasets/participant-datasets), [payments datasets](https://dataresearch.ndis.gov.au/datasets/payments-datasets), and their data-rules documents, comparing the June 2025 and June 2026 releases. Each file is pinned by size and SHA-256 checksum in `sources.csv`; set `BLOG_REFRESH_DATA=true` to force a fresh download and checksum validation. In the registry, `release_date` records the downloadable asset's Last-Modified date.

```{r}
#| label: source-manifest

source_manifest |>
  transmute(
    source = dataset,
    source_revision_date = release_date,
    coverage_end,
    file = local_file,
    bytes = comma(bytes),
    sha256_prefix = substr(sha256, 1, 12)
  ) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Source", "Source/revision date", "Coverage end", "Cached file", "Bytes", "SHA-256 prefix"))
```

:::
